lines: Your bank KYC expires today.
Update now or your account will be blocked: kyc-update.example/verify

drillBank.question: This text arrives in the morning, and your account works fine. What do you do?

options.text: Open the link and update it, just in case
options.why: A same-day deadline, a threat to block the account and a link: the pattern of a KYC scam. The page can take your details or install an app.

options.text: Leave the link, and check KYC in your bank's own app or at the branch
options.why: Banks give notice of KYC well ahead, and remind you after the due date. Whoever the sender seems to be, update only by a route you open yourself.

options.text: Reply to ask whether it is real
options.why: The reply goes to whoever sent the text, and they will say yes.

drillBank.cueSource: RBI press release 'RBI cautions against frauds in the name of KYC updation', 2 Feb 2024 (https://www.rbi.org.in/Scripts/BS_PressReleaseDisplay.aspx?prid=57244): false urgency and threats to freeze or block the account, apps installed through links in messages, and the advice to contact the bank directly and not to click suspicious or unverified links. RBI FAQs on the Master Direction on KYC, 9 Jun 2025, Q27–Q29 (https://www.rbi.org.in/commonman/Upload/English/FAQs/PDFs/KYC09062025.pdf): banks give advance notice and reminders after the due date, close accounts only after due notice, and customers should use utmost caution with links in KYC texts and emails. Both read on 22 Sep 2026. sourceIds: rbi-kyc-2024, rbi-kyc-faq.

lines: Your own payment code
Whoever scans this pays you.

drillBank.question: A friend owes you ₹300 for lunch and asks how to pay you back. Your app shows this. What do you do?

options.text: Show your code and let your friend scan it
options.why: Being paid needs only your code or your number. No scan, no PIN and no fingerprint from you.

options.text: Scan your friend's code and approve it, to receive
options.why: Scanning and approving pays out, by PIN, fingerprint or face. That is the refund-code trick.

options.text: Refuse, and ask for cash, since codes are risky
options.why: Showing your own code to a friend is how being paid by UPI works. Nothing leaves your account.

drillBank.cueSource: NPCI BHIM UPI brand guidelines (https://www.npci.org.in/uploads/BHIM_UPI_Guidelines_2026_012a0b1bce.pdf, as cited by the lesson, accessed 21 Sep 2026): only sending money requires the UPI PIN, and a QR code is shared to be paid and scanned to pay. NPCI UPI OC-226/2025-26, 7 Oct 2025 (https://www.npci.org.in/uploads/UPI_OC_No_226_FY_2025_26_Introduction_of_Additional_Authentication_methods_in_UPI_42c3693399.pdf, text via the TeamLease RegTech summary because the PDF is an image): an on-device fingerprint or face may approve instead of the PIN, so any approval sends money. sourceIds: npci-upi-guidelines, npci-oc-226.

lines: To: Ostrakel Driving School
IBAN: new payee
Name check: not possible.

drillBank.question: The invoice for your first driving lessons came by email, with this IBAN. You have not paid this school before. What do you do?

options.text: Send it. The name check is only a formality
options.why: Not possible means nobody has confirmed the name. The money follows the IBAN, whoever holds it.

options.text: Cancel for good. A failed check means a scam
options.why: Not possible is not a no match. It says only that no check was made.

options.text: Check the IBAN with the school by a route you find yourself, then pay
options.why: Its website typed yourself, its phone or its front desk. No check means no confirmation. Where your bank shows no name check at all, as some outside the euro area may until July 2027, do the same.

drillBank.cueSource: ECB, Instant Payments Regulation page (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/paym/retail/instant_payments/html/instant_payments_regulation.en.html, read 22 Sep 2026): verification of payee returns one of four results (match, close match, no match, other), covers standard and instant transfers, is required of euro-area providers from 9 Oct 2025, and of non-euro-area providers from 9 Jul 2027. Regulation (EU) 2024/886, Article 5c (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/886/oj). sourceIds: ecb-ipr, eu-2024-886.

lines: To: Lirmavik Rowing Club
Name check: match.
You paid this account in March.

drillBank.question: At training, the treasurer asked every member in person for the €45 season fee, to the account the club used in March. What do you do?

options.text: Cancel, since any transfer could be a scam
options.why: You heard it in person, and the check agrees. Refusing this one protects nothing.

options.text: Check the amount and the name, then confirm
options.why: An in-person request, a match and an account you paid before: an ordinary payment. Where a bank runs no name check yet, the other two still hold.

options.text: Ask the treasurer to confirm it by email first
options.why: You already heard it from her in person. An email adds a route that can be faked.

drillBank.cueSource: ECB, Instant Payments Regulation page (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/paym/retail/instant_payments/html/instant_payments_regulation.en.html, read 22 Sep 2026): a match means the name given agrees with the holder of the account behind the IBAN, and the check is required in the euro area from 9 Oct 2025 and outside it by 9 Jul 2027. It complements the lesson's quiz Q2, where the treasurer's change arrives by email. sourceIds: ecb-ipr.

lines: To: Velquist Phones
Name check: match.
Speed: instant
Reference: order 4471

drillBank.question: An online shop sells this phone at 60% below other shops, and its checkout offers instant transfer only. The name check says match. What do you do?

options.text: Send it. The name check says match
options.why: A match proves whose account it is. It says nothing about whether a phone will arrive.

options.text: Stop. A price far below other shops and a transfer-only checkout are the tells
options.why: A match says whose account it is, not that the shop will deliver. Once sent, an instant transfer cannot be taken back.

options.text: Send half now and the rest on delivery
options.why: Half sent to a shop that never delivers is still gone.

drillBank.cueSource: European Consumer Centre Czechia, 'ECC: warnings against practices in the sales period', 28 Nov 2025 (https://evropskyspotrebitel.gov.cz/news/ecc-warnings-agaist-practices-in-the-sales-period/): before a first purchase, check whether the seller is identified and whether there are payment options other than bank transfer. CCPC Ireland, 'Fake online shops' (https://www.ccpc.ie/manage-your-money/scams-and-frauds/common-scams/fake-online-shops): large discounts and unusual payment methods are warning signs. PSD2 Article 80 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2015/2366/oj): a payment order cannot be revoked once received. Regulation (EU) 2024/886, Article 5a: ten seconds. sourceIds: ecc-cz-2025, ccpc-fake-shops, psd2.

revised.title: Rent and bills as a share of net pay
revised.answers: What share of my net pay would this room take, bills included?
revised.short: How much of my pay goes on rent and bills?
revised.intro: Answers one question: rent and bills together, what share of your net pay do they take?

inputs.label: Net pay a month
inputs.hint: What reaches your account from work in a normal month. Paid 13 or 14 times a year? Add up a year's net pay and divide by 12. Leave out any housing allowance and take it off the rent instead: Eurostat counts it that way.
inputs.source: example: eu/money-basics/moving-out (situation and worked example, €1,125)
inputs.validation: id rs-netPay, min="0", no max. Read with toNumber. Blank, 0 or negative (a link can carry −100): error 'Enter your net pay a month, more than 0.' under the field, tied with aria-describedby, aria-invalid=true; the Figure, both 40% facts and the share sentence are replaced (see resultSentence); the day-one fold still works. A link value longer than 24 characters is ignored (kit rule).

inputs.label: Rent a month, your share
inputs.hint: The rent in the listing or contract. If it already includes some bills (an all-in or warm rent), put only the bills it leaves out under Bills. Weekly rent: multiply by 52 and divide by 12.
inputs.source: example: eu/money-basics/moving-out (document line 'Rent', €520 a month)
inputs.validation: id rs-rent, min="0". Blank counts as 0 with no error. Negative: error 'Enter 0 or more.' tied with aria-describedby and aria-invalid, and the value counts as 0 in every sum (housingShare and dayOneCost also clamp).

inputs.label: Bills a month, your share
inputs.hint: Your share of water, electricity, gas and heating, plus any refuse or building charges you pay, if the rent does not include them. Not your phone or internet. Ask the current tenants.
inputs.source: example: eu/money-basics/moving-out (document line 'Bills', about €80 a month)
inputs.validation: id rs-bills, min="0". Blank counts as 0. Negative: 'Enter 0 or more.', counts as 0.

inputs.label: Deposit due at the start
inputs.hint: The amount in the listing or contract, returned at the end if nothing is owed. The lesson's example is two months' rent, 2 × €520. Most countries cap it and count it on rent without bills; if you may pay it in parts, enter the part due at the start.
inputs.source: example: eu/money-basics/moving-out (document line 'Deposit', two months' rent, €1,040)
inputs.validation: Inside the day-one fold. id rs-deposit, min="0", no max (a fixed cap in euros breaks when the select is on ₹ or ₦). Blank counts as 0. Negative: 'Enter 0 or more.', counts as 0. At 0 the ledger row is hidden.

inputs.label: First month's rent paid in advance
inputs.hint: Whether the first month's rent is due on the day you collect the keys, on top of the deposit. The contract says.
inputs.source: example: eu/money-basics/moving-out (document line 'First month: In advance')
inputs.validation: Inside the day-one fold. A <select id="rs-firstMonthUpfront"> built with the kit's SelectField, options value 'yes' (text 'Yes, with the deposit') and 'no' (text 'No'). Read as upfront = fields.firstMonthUpfront !== 'no'; any other value (a link's ?firstMonthUpfront=evil, blank) falls back to yes, and the select is rendered with the normalised value so it never shows an empty choice.

inputs.label: Moving and connecting the bills
inputs.hint: Moving your things and connecting the bills: a one-off amount. The lesson's example is €60 + €80.
inputs.source: example: eu/money-basics/moving-out details (€60 to connect the bills, €80 to move)
inputs.validation: Inside the day-one fold. id rs-moveCosts, min="0". Blank counts as 0. Negative: 'Enter 0 or more.', counts as 0. At 0 the ledger row is hidden.

inputs.label: Saved so far
inputs.hint: What you could use on day one without borrowing.
inputs.source: example: not in the lesson; chosen so the fold opens on a difference to read. Labelled with the rest as an example, not a prediction.
inputs.validation: Inside the day-one fold. id rs-saved, min="0". Blank counts as 0. Negative: 'Enter 0 or more.', counts as 0.

revised.resultSentence:
Monthly sentence (exactly one, in p.plain), by branch. {netPay}, {housing}, {left} and {gap} use exact(); {share} is percent(ratio, locale, 1), or 'just over 40%' / 'just under 40%' when that prints 40.0% but the position is over or under.
(1) Net pay 0, blank or negative: 'Enter your net pay a month, more than 0, to see what share rent and bills take.'
(2) Net pay above 0, rent and bills both 0: 'Enter the rent and bills to see what share of your {netPay} net pay they take.'
(3) left > 0: 'Rent and bills of {housing} take {share} of your {netPay} net pay, leaving {left} for everything else.' Example: 'Rent and bills of €600 take 53.3% of your €1,125 net pay, leaving €525 for everything else.' Near the line: 'Rent and bills of €450.01 take just over 40% of your €1,125 net pay, leaving €674.99 for everything else.'
(4) left = 0: 'Rent and bills of {housing} take all of your {netPay} net pay, leaving nothing for anything else.'
(5) left < 0: 'Rent and bills of {housing} are {|left|} more than your {netPay} net pay.' Example at 500/520/80: 'Rent and bills of €600 are €100 more than your €500 net pay.'
The 40% comparison is never in the sentence; it lives in the facts: '{gap} over it' when position is over and |gap| ≥ 0.01; '{|gap|} under it' when under; 'exactly at it; Eurostat counts only more than 40%' when at; 'less than €0.01 over it' / 'less than €0.01 under it' (the 0.01 formatted with money(0.01, locale, 2)) when the position is over or under but the rounded gap is 0.
Day-one sentence (one, inside the fold): (a) total = 0: 'Nothing is entered as due before the first payday.' (b) gap > 0 and saved > 0: 'Moving in takes {total} before the first payday, {gap} more than the {saved} saved.' Example: 'Moving in takes €1,700 before the first payday, €500 more than the €1,200 saved.' (c) gap > 0 and saved = 0: 'Moving in takes {total} before the first payday, and nothing is entered as saved yet.' (d) gap < 0: 'Moving in takes {total} before the first payday; the {saved} saved covers it, with {|gap|} left.' (e) gap = 0 and total > 0: 'Moving in takes {total} before the first payday, exactly the {saved} saved.' Never 'short', 'fails', 'too much', 'can't afford' or 'overburdened' about the reader.
revised.maths:
All in src/lib/finance.ts, pure, integer-cent arithmetic.
Shared helpers (exported, and src/lib/lesson-math.ts imports round2 instead of its private copy at line 193): round1(n) = Math.round(n × 10) / 10; round2(n) = Math.round(n × 100) / 100 (the shared money rounding); toCents(n) = Number.isFinite(n) && n > 0 ? Math.round(n × 100) : 0, so negatives, NaN and Infinity count as 0.
housingShare(netPay: number, rent: number, bills: number, linePercent: number): { housing: number; left: number | null; ratio: number | null; share: number | null; line: number | null; gap: number | null; position: 'over' | 'at' | 'under' | null }.
 n = toCents(netPay); h = toCents(rent) + toCents(bills); housing = h / 100.
 If n === 0 (0, blank or negative net pay): return { housing, left: null, ratio: null, share: null, line: null, gap: null, position: null }.
 ratio = h / n (unrounded; the island prints percent(ratio, locale, 1)). share = round1(ratio × 100), used by tests and the 'just over/under' check.
 lineC = Math.round(n × linePercent / 100); line = lineC / 100.
 cmp = h × 100 − n × linePercent, exact in integers because linePercent is a whole number (a regions test asserts Number.isInteger(line.value)). position = cmp > 0 ? 'over' : cmp === 0 ? 'at' : 'under'. The position is decided on these unrounded values, never on the rounded share or line.
 gap = (h − lineC) / 100, signed. It can be 0 while position is 'over' or 'under' when the true difference is under a cent (net pay 1,125.01, housing 450): the island then prints 'less than €0.01 under it'.
 left = (n − h) / 100, signed; negative means rent and bills exceed net pay (share above 100%).
dayOneCost(rent: number, deposit: number, firstMonthUpfront: boolean, moveCosts: number, saved: number): { deposit; firstMonth; moveCosts; total; saved; gap: number; position: 'more' | 'exact' | 'covered' }.
 r, d, m, s = toCents of each; f = firstMonthUpfront ? r : 0; t = d + f + m; g = t − s. Returns each / 100, total = t / 100, gap = g / 100 (positive when day one needs more than is saved), position = g > 0 ? 'more' : g === 0 ? 'exact' : 'covered'.
Island (src/islands/RentShare.tsx) on useFields('rs', defaults), useLocale, NumberField, SelectField, Figure, Result, Fact, HowItWorks, ToolActions. It reads every field with toNumber, sets field errors as in inputs, and passes the raw numbers (the functions clamp). linePercent comes only from the `line` prop (region.tools.rentShare.line.value from the page's edition), never from the locale. The 'just over/under' swap: when position !== 'at' and percent(ratio, locale, 1) === percent(line.value / 100, locale, 1). The Figure and the main monthly row carry loss only when left < 0; no other element ever carries is-loss.

revised.howItWorks:
Rent and bills = rent + bills. Share of net pay = rent and bills ÷ net pay. Left after rent and bills = net pay − rent − bills. The line = 40% × net pay.

The 40% comes from Eurostat, the EU's statistics office. It counts a household as overburdened when its total housing costs, net of housing allowances, come to more than 40% of its disposable income (Eurostat glossary, checked 22 September 2026). Two things differ here, as in the lesson: your net pay stands in for the household's disposable income, and the sum is done for one month. The line is a statistic about households, not a limit or a verdict on a room. Exactly 40% is not counted as overburdened, because the definition says more than 40%. The question that matters is whether what is left covers food, travel, your phone and a buffer; the budget planner works that out. In 2025, 9.1% of people aged 15 to 29 in the EU lived in a household above the line, against 7.7% of all people (Eurostat, housing cost overburden rate by age, updated 17 September 2026).

What this does not count: anyone else's income in your household; pay that comes 13 or 14 times a year, unless you enter a year's net pay divided by 12; a housing allowance, unless you leave it out of net pay and take it off the rent as the hint says; bills already inside an all-in rent, which belong in the rent only; rises in rent or bills; and the rest of your month.

Moving in: due before the first payday = the deposit due at the start + the first month's rent, if it is asked in advance + moving and connecting the bills, set against what you have saved. The deposit comes back at the end if nothing is owed, so until then it is money you cannot spend. Deposit rules are national. France caps the deposit at one month's rent without charges for an unfurnished home and two for a furnished one (Service-Public.fr, verified 9 June 2026). German law caps it at three months' rent without operating costs and lets a tenant pay it in three monthly parts, the first at the start (BGB § 551). Your national housing or consumer authority states the rule where you rent.

Before you pay anything: pay nothing before a viewing and a signed contract. If a listing asks for money first, report it to the portal. If you have paid, tell the police and, if you paid by card or direct debit, your bank at once. A European Consumer Centre advises free of charge when the business is in another EU country, Norway or Iceland.

Currency: the share and the line are the same in any currency. The select changes the symbol among the currencies it lists; for złoty, kronor or another currency it does not list, type the amounts as they are and read the share and the line, which do not depend on the symbol.

One sentence and one question (skeptic 2 over skeptic 1): skeptic 1 rewrote the result as a sentence carrying the 40% line and day one; skeptic 2 required one sentence. The hard limit is one sentence, so the sentence carries only share and what is left; the line comparison is a fact row with skeptic 1's attribution wording; day one moved into a closed <details> fold 'What moving in costs before the first payday' with its own ledger and sentence, which never changes the monthly answer.
Day-one wording (skeptic 1): one version only, with branches for more, covered, exact, nothing saved and nothing due.

Deposit (both): months replaced by an amount, 'Deposit due at the start', default 1040 labelled as the lesson's example, row hidden at 0. The hint tells a reader who may pay in parts (Germany, BGB § 551, checked) to enter the part due at the start. I dropped skeptic 1's 'Often one to three months' because 'often' is unsourced and skeptic 2 asked for no norm-suggesting wording. I did not cap the field at 10,000 (skeptic 2): the months field it bounded is gone, and a euro cap breaks when the select is on ₹ or ₦. France's caps (1 month unfurnished, 2 furnished, without charges; Service-Public, verified 9 Jun 2026) and Germany's (3 months without operating costs, three parts) are in How this is worked out; Ireland and the Netherlands are not named because skeptic 2 could reach only secondary sources for them.

Double counting and bills definition (both): rent hint covers all-in and warm rents; bills hint adds refuse and building charges and excludes phone and internet (Eurostat glossary, checked); move costs and first-month hints added. The first-month hint says 'the contract says' instead of skeptic 1's unsourced 'many landlords'.

Housing allowance and 13th/14th-month pay (both): the net pay hint now leaves the allowance out of income and off the rent (Eurostat nets it out of both, checked) and turns 13 or 14 payments into a year's net pay ÷ 12; How this is worked out repeats both.

Attribution (both): the fact reads '40% of this net pay, the line Eurostat uses for households', with a notice that net pay stands in for household disposable income and that the line is a statistic, not a limit.

Verdict styling (skeptic 1): only the Figure and the main monthly row carry is-loss, and only when rent and bills exceed net pay (skeptic 2's share above 100%); line and day-one facts never do. The e2e pins assert zero is-loss at defaults and exactly two at 500/520/80.
short (both) becomes 'How much of my pay goes on rent and bills?'; I made the same change to `answers` ('…this room take, bills included?'), which had the same rent-only problem.
Percent formatting (skeptic 1): housingShare returns ratio; the island uses percent(ratio, locale, 1); share = round1(ratio × 100) is for tests only.

Select from links (skeptic 1): anything but 'no' reads as yes, and the select shows the normalised value. Id prefix is 'rs' (rs-firstMonthUpfront) rather than skeptic 1's 'rent', which would have made the rent field 'rent-rent'. e2e loads #firstMonthUpfront=evil and expects €1,700.
Privacy (skeptic 1): the fragment link from the registry's kit change, with the line under the buttons; this also covers the lesson hand-off.

Stale figures (skeptic 2), re-checked 22 Sep 2026 on the Eurostat API: overburden 15–29 is 9.1% in 2025 (9.7% in 2024), all people 7.7% (8.2%), ilc_lvho07a updated 17 Sep 2026; age leaving home 26.3 in 2025 (yth_demo_030, updated 16 Apr 2026), lowest Finland 21.3, highest Croatia 31.5 after checking all 27 member states. The tool copy uses 2025 figures, and lessonEdits refresh the lesson's details and sources.
ECC scoping (skeptic 2): How this is worked out uses the portal, then police and bank, then ECC only for a business in another EU country, Norway or Iceland (EVZ page checked, updated 27 Mar 2026).
risks: Proxy measure: Eurostat's line is for households' yearly disposable income net of allowances; the tool sets it against one person's monthly net pay, as the lesson does. The notice and How this is worked out say so. A content-reviewer should confirm the wording never implies Eurostat sets a limit for a person.

The day-one fold is a second calculation on the page. It sits in a closed fold that never moves the monthly answer. If a reviewer still counts it as a second question, it moves into its own tool unchanged (the dayOneCost function, its four fields and its pins).

lp:locale is one key for the whole site, so a reader who chose ₹ in the India edition sees the Europe tool in ₹ while the scenario and hints say €. This is existing kit behaviour for every calculator. The 40% line is unaffected because it comes from the page's edition.
Non-euro EU currencies (PLN, SEK, CZK, HUF, DKK, RON) are still missing from the select, against the aim in docs/REGIONAL_TEACHING.md. Adding them is a site-wide decision.

Figures move: the 2025 Eurostat values and the French and German deposit rules are dated. The regions test fails the build when the Rule's asOf is more than 12 months old. The copy-only figures in How this is worked out need the same yearly check.
The lesson's 31.6% renters figure could not be re-checked for 2025 (the API refused the query). The content-reviewer should confirm it before the details refresh ships.
Schema growth: moreTools and the deduction handoff are new lesson keys. If they are left out of the collectStrings skip sets, keys such as 'netPay' would be counted as reader words.
The registry's RulesLine lead 'Rules as of' would call a statistic a rule on this page. The neutral 'Checked {date}:' lead must land in the shared component before rent-share ships.

revised.title: Tax on side income and fees
revised.answers: How much tax is left to set aside, or can come back, on what my own work brought in?
revised.short: What tax is left on my side income?
revised.intro: Answers one question: after the tax already taken or paid, how much is left to set aside, or can come back?

inputs.label: Tax deducted on your fees, as your statement shows it
inputs.hint: Part B of your Annual Information Statement lists what each payer deducted in your name for the year you are filing for. Form 26AS shows the same.
inputs.source: https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/all-topics/e-filing-services/ais-annual-information-statement (Part B: TDS/TCS; accessed 22 Sep 2026). Default: in/money-basics/tds-refund, Tax deposited ₹15,000
inputs.validation: India edition only. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Above 1,000,000,000,000: 'That figure is larger than this tool works with.' Blank counts as 0. A field in error is left out and the ledger total and sentence are hidden until it is fixed; the error text is tied to the field with aria-describedby and aria-invalid.

inputs.label: Other tax already paid in your name for that year
inputs.hint: Tax deducted from a salary or interest, and any advance or self-assessment tax you paid. The year's return counts them all.
inputs.source: https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/all-topics/e-filing-services/tax-payments (advance and self-assessment tax; accessed 22 Sep 2026)
inputs.validation: India only. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Too large: as above. Blank counts as 0.

inputs.label: Tax due on that year's whole income
inputs.hint: The tax your return worked out. If you have not filed yet, the department's Income and Tax Calculator estimates it; nothing here chooses a regime. On the lesson's ₹1,50,000, with no other income, it is ₹0.
inputs.source: https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/income-tax-calculator (the department's Income and Tax Calculator; accessed 22 Sep 2026). This tool never works tax out.
inputs.validation: India only. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Too large: as above. Blank counts as 0.

inputs.label: Deducted but not yet on your statement
inputs.hint: A payer that has not filed it yet. Once it corrects its filing, the credit can be claimed, on a revised return or a rectification request.
inputs.source: https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/all-topics/e-filing-services/tds-compliance (deductor files a revised TDS return) and https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/all-topics/e-filing-services/rectification-request-tax-credit-mismatch (both accessed 22 Sep 2026)
inputs.validation: India only. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Too large: as above. Blank counts as 0. It never enters the sum; above 0 it shows as a fact.

inputs.label: Fees invoiced for that year
inputs.hint: Optional, inside a fold headed 'Check against your invoices'. It checks the statement and never changes the answer.
inputs.source: example: in/money-basics/tds-refund (₹1,50,000 invoiced)
inputs.validation: India only. Blank means not given: no check fact. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Too large: as above. An error here withholds only the check fact, never the ledger.

inputs.label: Paid into your account for those invoices
inputs.hint: What actually reached you for them.
inputs.source: example: in/money-basics/tds-refund (₹1,35,000 arrived)
inputs.validation: India only. Blank means not given. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Above invoiced (both given): 'More arrived than was invoiced. Check both figures.' on this field. An error here withholds only the check fact.

inputs.label: Money in from the work this year
inputs.hint: Tutoring, gigs and sales, before any fees. It counts whether or not a Form 1099-K arrives for it.
inputs.source: example: us/start-something/se-tax ($3,400 tutoring + $2,600 resale); https://www.irs.gov/businesses/gig-economy-tax-center (last reviewed 9 Jul 2026)
inputs.validation: US only. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Above 1,000,000,000,000: 'That figure is larger than this tool works with.' Blank counts as 0. When 92.35% of profit, rounded to the dollar, is above 200,000: 'Above $200,000 of net earnings, about $216,600 of profit, an extra 0.9% Medicare tax can apply, so this sum stops being complete. IRS Topic 554 explains it.' on this field, and no result is shown.

inputs.label: Costs of the work
inputs.hint: Shipping, packaging, platform fees: only what your records show. Not things you keep.
inputs.source: example: us/start-something/se-tax ($600 shipping and packaging + $400 marketplace fees)
inputs.validation: US only. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Too large: as above. Blank counts as 0. Above money in is not an error: the loss sentence shows.

inputs.label: Income tax, % of profit, if any (an example)
inputs.hint: Often nil in a first year of side work: in 2026 the standard deduction takes the first $16,100 of income, or your earned income plus $450 if someone can claim you as a dependent. Try 10%, the lesson's example, to see a year with some due.
inputs.source: Typed by the reader; 0 by default. Standard deduction: https://www.irs.gov/node/151941 (IR-2025-103, 9 Oct 2025) and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 s.3.14 https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf. 10% is the se-tax lesson's labelled example.
inputs.validation: US only. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Above 100: 'A rate cannot be more than 100%.' Blank counts as 0.

inputs.label: Already paid toward this work's tax
inputs.hint: Estimated payments you sent for it, or extra withholding you asked a job to take on your Form W-4. Not the Social Security, Medicare or income tax a job takes for its own pay.
inputs.source: https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/estimated-taxes (last updated 28 Jun 2026)
inputs.validation: US only. Below 0: 'Enter 0 or more.' Too large: as above. Blank counts as 0. More than the tax worked out is not an error: the 'more has been paid' branch shows.

rules.label: Share of net profit counted as net earnings from self-employment (Schedule SE line 4a), %
rules.sourceTitle: IRS, 2025 Instructions for Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 4a; page last reviewed 30 Apr 2026. Recheck when the 2026 edition is published. Topic 554 (26 May 2026) gives the same 92.35%.

rules.label: Net earnings from self-employment (Schedule SE line 4c, after the 92.35%) at which the tax applies, $; tested on the whole-dollar line, so it starts at $432.60 of profit
rules.sourceTitle: IRS, 2025 Instructions for Schedule SE: 'You must file Schedule SE if the amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more' (last reviewed 30 Apr 2026). Not Topic 554 or the SE-tax page, whose wording reads as a test on profit.

rules.label: Social Security part of self-employment tax, %
rules.sourceTitle: IRS, Self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare taxes): 15.3%, of which 12.4% for social security and 2.9% for Medicare (last reviewed 27 Jun 2026)

rules.label: Medicare part of self-employment tax, %, on all net earnings
rules.sourceTitle: IRS, Self-employment tax (Social Security and Medicare taxes) (last reviewed 27 Jun 2026)

rules.label: Most wages and net earnings together that the 12.4% Social Security part applies to, 2026, $
rules.sourceTitle: IRS Topic no. 751: 'For earnings in 2026, this base limit is $184,500' (updated 20 Jan 2026). The SE-tax page still quotes 2024's $168,600 and ssa.gov returned 403, so the IRS topic is the cited source.

rules.label: Net earnings above which the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax can apply (single filers); the tool shows an error and no result above it, $
rules.sourceTitle: IRS Topic no. 554, Self-employment tax: $200,000 for all others than married filers (updated 26 May 2026)

rules.label: Tax owed on filing, after withholding and credits, from which the IRS generally expects payments during the year, $
rules.sourceTitle: IRS, Estimated taxes: $1,000 test, the no-prior-year-liability exception (US citizen or resident all year, 12-month year) (last updated 28 Jun 2026); dates from Manage taxes for your gig work (last reviewed 28 Jun 2026)

rules.label: Standard deduction, single filer, tax year 2026, $ (cited in the hint and How this is worked out; not used in the maths)
rules.sourceTitle: IRS, IR-2025-103, IRS releases tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2026 (9 Oct 2025); Rev. Proc. 2025-32 s.3.14(1)

rules.label: Standard deduction floor for someone who can be claimed as a dependent, 2026, $ (copy only)
rules.sourceTitle: IRS, Rev. Proc. 2025-32 s.3.14(2): the greater of $1,350 or $450 plus earned income, for taxable years beginning in 2026

rules.label: Amount added to a dependent's earned income for the standard deduction, 2026, $ (copy only)
Tax for a year, after tax deducted at source, from which advance tax is due during that year, ₹ (Section 404, Income-tax Act 2025; section 208 of the 1961 Act for 2025-26 income)
rules.sourceTitle: Income Tax Department, Tax Payments: 'advance tax is payable if the amount of tax payable during the year ... is Rs. 10,000 or more'; instalment dates, and all by 15 March under the presumptive scheme (page undated; accessed 22 Sep 2026)

rules.label: Interest on advance tax not paid or paid short, % a month (Section 424 of the 2025 Act, 234B of the 1961 Act); deferment interest can be 1% or 3%, so copy says 'from 1% a month'
rules.sourceTitle: Income Tax Department, Tax Payments and Tax Payments FAQ (undated; accessed 22 Sep 2026)

rules.label: Last day for a belated return for 2025-26 income (assessment year 2026-27), as yyyymmdd, or earlier if assessment is completed first; an updated return cannot increase a refund. Carries expires: 2026-12-31
rules.sourceTitle: Income Tax Department, Income tax returns: 'on or before 31st December 2026, or prior to the completion of the assessment, whichever occurs earlier'; 'The updated return cannot result in ... increase in refund' (accessed 22 Sep 2026)

outputs: No Figure headline: the answer is the double-ruled total of the ledger itself (the kit's rule; CompoundGrowth and BudgetPlanner do the same), so the wording fixes for the headline live on the total's label.

US ledger 1, heading 'Profit from the work': Money in $6,000; − Costs of the work $1,000; = Net profit $5,000, closed with the double rule. A negative net profit prints in the loss colour with the word 'loss' in its label ('Net loss'), never colour alone.

US ledger 2, heading 'Tax on it' (not shown when profit is 0): Self-employment tax $707 with the caption '15.3% of $4,618, which is 92.35% of $5,000, rounded to the dollar' (below the line: '92.35% of $X is $Y, under $400, so none is due', value $0); + Income tax at your example 0% $0; = Tax on these figures $707 (single rule, subtotal); − Already paid toward it $0; = To set aside on these figures $707 (double rule). When more is paid than the tax, the last row reads 'Paid beyond this sum' with the excess. The $4,618 base is a caption, not a row, so the rows add up.

US facts under ledger 2: 'Self-employment tax is 14.1% of profit, set by law' (plus ', plus your example 10%' when the rate is above 0), only when profit and self-employment tax are above 0; the estimated-tax fact when the tax on these figures is $1,000 or more; and always one scope line: 'Federal tax only, before the standard deduction and the deduction for half of self-employment tax, so the income tax line can overstate. Wages from a job count toward the same Social Security cap.'

US estimated-tax fact: 'The IRS generally expects tax paid during the year from people who will owe $1,000 or more after withholding and credits: by April 15, June 15, September 15 and January 15 of the next year, or the next business day if one falls on a weekend or holiday. None is needed if you had no tax liability last year, were a US citizen or resident all year, and that year was 12 months.' Dates held as month-day pairs and written with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { month: 'long', day: 'numeric', timeZone: 'UTC' }); links to the estimated-taxes and gig-work pages with their 28 June 2026 review dates.

India ledger, heading 'For the year you are filing for': Tax deducted on your fees, on your statement ₹15,000; + Other tax already paid in your name ₹0; = Tax on record in your name ₹15,000 (single rule, subtotal); − Tax due on that year's whole income ₹0; = Can come back on that year's return ₹15,000 (double rule). Still-to-pay branch: the last row reads 'Still to pay, before any interest' ₹X. Equal: 'Nothing comes back, nothing to pay' ₹0.

India facts: the belated-return fact whenever a result shows ('For 2025-26 income, a belated return can be filed until 31 December 2026, or before assessment if that comes first. An updated return filed after that cannot increase a refund.'); the missing-credit fact when above 0 ('₹6,000 deducted but not yet on your statement is not in this sum. It can count once the payer corrects its filing, claimed on a revised return or a rectification request.'); the invoice check fact when both invoice fields are given (match: 'Invoices minus what arrived: ₹15,000, the same as the tax on your statement.', or '... the same as the tax on your statement plus what is still missing.'; mismatch: 'Invoices minus what arrived: ₹X. That is not the tax on your statement. The gap can also be GST, platform or bank fees, or a payment not yet made; only the statement's figure comes back.'); and the advance-tax fact when still to pay is ₹10,000 or more ('When a year's tax, after tax deducted at source, is ₹10,000 or more, it is due in advance during that year: by 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March, or all by 15 March under the presumptive scheme. Interest, from 1% a month, can be added when it is paid late.'), dates written with Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-IN').
A one-sentence plain result under the ledgers (see resultSentence).

Above the Copy link and Share buttons, for this tool only: 'The link carries the figures you typed, after a #, so they are never sent to this site. Share it only if you are happy for others to see them.'
No Currency field. Money is always ₹ with en-IN grouping on /in and $ with en-US on /us, whatever lp:locale holds.

Page, HTML only, no JS: the scenario line per edition ('It opens on an example: the internship in the lesson on getting TDS back: ₹15,000 withheld from ₹1,50,000 of fees, on an income that owed no tax.' / 'It opens on an example: the lesson's year of tutoring and reselling: $6,000 in, $1,000 of costs, and no other income.'); a 'Figures this uses' list from region.rules (label, value, source link, 'checked' date via Intl for the edition); for India, the Act line 'For 2025-26 income (Income-tax Act, 1961): the Annual Information Statement and Form 26AS. For income from 1 April 2026 (Income-tax Act, 2025, tax year 2026-27): the Annual Information Statement in Form No. 168.' sourced to the TDS compliance page, accessed 22 Sep 2026; 'Lessons that use this' (in/money-basics/tds-refund; us/start-something/se-tax); the education-not-advice note.

revised.maths:
Shared helper, new file src/lib/money-math.ts: toCents(amount: number): number = Math.round(amount * 100), which is exact for typed amounts with up to two decimals; fromCents(cents) = cents / 100. Every sum below runs on integer cents or whole dollars. Every product with a rate is one integer numerator divided once, so a .5 tie is represented exactly and Math.round takes it up, with no epsilon. Rates held as printed are turned into integers inside the function: 92.35 → 9235 per 10,000; 12.4 → 124 and 2.9 → 29 per 1,000 (Math.round(rate * 10)); a typed rate r → Math.round(r * 100) per 10,000.

US, in src/lib/finance.ts: selfEmploymentSetAside(input: { moneyIn: number; costs: number; incomeTaxPercent: number; alreadyPaid: number }, rules: { seNetEarningsShare; seThreshold; seSocialSecurityRate; seMedicareRate; ssWageBase; additionalMedicareThreshold; estimatedTaxLine }): { net, loss, profit, netEarnings, seApplies, seTax, incomeTax, tax, balance, seShareOfProfit, beyondScope, expectDuringYear }.
1. netC = toCents(moneyIn) − toCents(costs); net = netC / 100 (may be below 0); loss = netC < 0.
2. profitC = max(0, netC); profit = profitC / 100.
3. netEarnings = Math.round(profitC * 9235 / 1,000,000), in whole dollars (Schedule SE line 4a, rounded).
4. seApplies = netEarnings ≥ 400. The test is on the rounded line, the same convention as the count, so the tax starts at a profit of $432.60. That start is derived, not held: Math.ceil((400 − 0.5) * 1,000,000 / 9235) / 100 = 432.6; the copy says 'about $433 of profit'.
5. seTax = seApplies ? Math.round((min(netEarnings, ssWageBase) * 124 + netEarnings * 29) / 1000) : 0, in whole dollars. The 12.4% stops at the 2026 base of $184,500; the 2.9% has no cap. One rounding of the combined figure matches the lesson's '15.3% of $4,618 = $707'. Schedule SE rounds line by line, which can differ by $1; How this is worked out says so.
6. beyondScope = netEarnings > 200,000. The island shows the error and no result, because the 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax is not modelled. The function still returns its figures, for the tests.
7. incomeTax = Math.round(profitC * Math.round(incomeTaxPercent * 100) / 1,000,000), in whole dollars, at the reader's example rate on profit. No bracket, standard deduction or half-SE deduction is modelled; those rules are cited copy only.
8. tax = seTax + incomeTax; balanceC = tax * 100 − toCents(alreadyPaid); balance = balanceC / 100 (below 0 when more has been paid than this sum).
9. seShareOfProfit = (profitC > 0 && seTax > 0) ? Math.round(seTax * 100,000 / profitC) / 10 : null: a percent to one decimal, never NaN or Infinity.
10. expectDuringYear = tax ≥ 1,000. It is tested on the tax on these figures, before anything already paid, because estimated payments are how the IRS line is met, not an exemption from it.

India, in src/lib/finance.ts: tdsBalance(input: { tdsOnStatement: number; otherCredits: number; taxDue: number; missing: number; invoiced: number | null; arrived: number | null }, rules: { advanceTaxLine }): { credits, balance, comesBack, stillToPay, missing, gap, gapMatches, advanceTaxDue }.
1. creditsC = toCents(tdsOnStatement) + toCents(otherCredits); credits = creditsC / 100.
2. balanceC = creditsC − toCents(taxDue); balance = balanceC / 100; comesBack = max(0, balanceC) / 100; stillToPay = max(0, −balanceC) / 100.
3. missing is returned unchanged and never enters the sum: it is not on the statement, so it cannot come back yet.
4. gap = (invoiced !== null && arrived !== null) ? (toCents(invoiced) − toCents(arrived)) / 100 : null. The island passes null for a blank field. gapMatches = gap === null ? null : (toCents(invoiced) − toCents(arrived)) === toCents(tdsOnStatement) + toCents(missing).
5. advanceTaxDue = stillToPay ≥ 10,000. It is shown only as a fact. When it is true, the tax net of every credit is at least ₹10,000, so the year's tax after TDS certainly crossed the advance-tax line.
No slab, regime, rebate, presumptive rate or TDS rate is held.

Island validation (not in the pure functions): parse with the kit's toNumber. Below 0 gives 'Enter 0 or more.' Above 1e12 gives 'That figure is larger than this tool works with.' (this keeps integer cents under Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER). A rate above 100 gives 'A rate cannot be more than 100%.' Arrived above invoiced (both given) gives 'More arrived than was invoiced. Check both figures.' US netEarnings above 200,000 puts the Topic 554 error on Money in. Any error outside the optional invoice pair hides the ledger totals and the sentence.

Edge cases:
- Money in equal to costs: the 'no profit' branch.
- Costs above money in: the loss branch, with ledger 2 not shown.
- Money in and costs both 0: the prompt branch.
- Profit under $432.60: no self-employment tax, and the sentence says income tax may still apply.
- Already paid above the tax: the 'more has been paid' branch.

revised.howItWorks:
United States:
- money in − costs of the work = net profit
- net earnings = 92.35% of net profit, rounded to the dollar. This is Schedule SE's line 4a: 100% less the 7.65% an employer would pay.
- Self-employment tax is due once net earnings reach $400 in a year, about $433 of profit. It is 12.4% for Social Security on net earnings up to $184,500 in 2026, plus 2.9% for Medicare on all of them, rounded to the dollar.
- income tax = your example % of net profit
- to set aside = self-employment tax + income tax − what you have already paid toward it

The rates are set by law and come from the IRS pages listed under 'Figures this uses', each with the date it was checked. The income tax share is only your example.

What this does not work out:
- The standard deduction. In 2026 it is $16,100, or your earned income plus $450 if someone can claim you as a dependent, which is why income tax is often nil in a first year.
- The deduction for half of self-employment tax.
Because of these two, the income tax line can overstate.

It also leaves out:
- State income tax (usa.gov/state-taxes).
- The 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax, which is why the tool stops above $200,000 of net earnings.
- Wages from a job, which use up part of the same Social Security cap.

Schedule SE rounds line by line, which can differ from this by a dollar. Your return works out the real figure, and the IRS estimated taxes page explains how to estimate it during the year. With a job as well, the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator can take side income into account. It needs a W-2 job or a pension, so it does not help with side income alone.

India:
- tax on record = tax deducted on your fees, as your statement shows it, + other tax already paid in your name for that year (tax deducted from salary or interest, advance or self-assessment tax)
- can come back = tax on record − tax due on that year's whole income

A figure below zero is still to pay, before any interest for paying late. When that is ₹10,000 or more, advance tax was due during the year, and interest from 1% a month can be added.

Only credits on record are refunded. Tax deducted but not yet on your statement is shown on its own: it can count once the payer corrects its filing, claimed on a revised return or a rectification request.

Invoices minus what arrived is only a check. The gap can be tax, but also:
- GST billed on top
- platform or bank fees
- a payment not yet made
Not every payment has tax deducted from it.

This tool never works out the tax due. It models no slab, regime, rebate or presumptive scheme. Your return gives that figure, or the department's Income and Tax Calculator estimates it.

It does not work out:
- interest or fees for filing or paying late
- interest the department may add to a refund

A refund is processed only after the return is e-verified. It is paid only into a pre-validated bank account in the name on your PAN.

For 2025-26 income (Income-tax Act, 1961), a belated return can be filed until 31 December 2026, and an updated return cannot increase a refund. The statements for that year are the Annual Information Statement and Form 26AS. For income from 1 April 2026 (Income-tax Act, 2025, tax year 2026-27), the statement is the Annual Information Statement in Form No. 168.

Links, each with its access date: incometax.gov.in's Income and Tax Calculator, Income tax returns, Refund status, TDS compliance, Tax payments and Rectification pages.

Both editions: for learning only. This is not tax advice, and the numbers it opens with are the lessons' examples.

risks: Tax-advice perception: the only rates held are US constants set in law. India's tax due and the US income-tax share are typed by the reader, with the US share at 0 by default. revised.resultSentence: No score or total is kept. After each reveal the status line reads 'Correct.', 'Not quite.' or, when nothing was picked, 'No pick this time, so this one comes back tomorrow.', and the reveal names the sign and which way the money or details would move. After the first reveal that saves on this device (saveProgress returns true), one line appears under the list: 'Situations you answered here come back from {date}.', where {date} is the earliest due date among this page's six check ids, formatted with the edition locale as weekday, day and month (en-IN and en-IE 'Wednesday, 23 September'; en-US 'Wednesday, September 23'). Zero case: a reader who reveals nothing sees no line. JavaScript off, storage blocked or a failed save: the line stays hidden and nothing is scheduled, while every reveal still works. revised.maths: No money is computed at run time. The page is static HTML plus the existing LessonScript module; there is no island. Pure functions, all unit-tested: (1) New src/lib/drills.ts mergeDrill(region, slug, lessonId, lessonScenarios, bankScenarios). It returns lessonScenarios.map((s, i) => ({ checkId: `${lessonId}#d${i + 1}`, screen: s.screen, check: s.check, ordinary: s.ordinary ?? false })) followed by bankScenarios.map((s) => ({ checkId: `${region}/tools/${slug}#${s.id}`, screen: s.screen, check: s.check, ordinary: s.ordinary })). The order is fixed, with no shuffling. (2) drillProblems(merged, { total: 6, ordinary: 2 }) returns string[], empty when fine: 'needs 6 situations' when length ≠ 6; 'needs exactly 2 ordinary' when the count of ordinary ≠ 2; 'duplicate check id'; 'answer out of range'. [tool].astro throws at build with these messages. (3) drillContext(screen, locale) is [`${from}:`, amount === undefined ? '' : money(amount, locale), ...lines, action ? `[${action}]` : ''].filter(Boolean).join(' '). checks.json.ts uses it for both bank and lesson drill checks, so the amount the reader saw is in the review context. (4) In src/lib/progress.ts schedule(progress, id, correct, now), a new first step: if correct and review[id] exists and review[id].due.slice(0, 10) > dayString(now), return progress unchanged (the same object), because an early right answer is not a spaced retrieval. Otherwise the existing rule applies: correct gives box min(5, box + 1), wrong gives box 1, due = today + BOX_DAYS[box] (1, 3, 7, 14, 30 days). (5) nextReturnAmong(progress, ids) returns the earliest due.slice(0, 10) among the ids present in progress.review, as dayToDate(day), or null when none is present. (6) isQuizCheck(id) = /#q\d+$/.test(id), replacing both id.includes('#q') tests in LessonScript. Figures on screens are integers, formatted by money(amount, edition locale) with 0 fraction digits; the bank schema caps amount at z.number().int().positive().max(10_000_000). The only sums in the text are fixed and pinned: in fake-check, 3,160 − 260 = 2,900 is sent, and after the bounce 3,160 − 2,900 − 3,160 = −2,900 is owed, so '$2,900' appears in the action and in a why. Edge cases: with no bank file for (edition, slug), there is no page and no index row, both from one drillExists predicate. If the bank is present but fromLesson is missing, in another edition, has no drill explorable or has no reportTo, the build throws. If drillProblems is non-empty, the build throws. A check id no longer in checks.json is skipped by Review (existing). With storage blocked or JavaScript off, nothing is scheduled and the return line stays hidden.

revised.howItWorks: How this is worked out. You see six made-up messages about work: the three from the lesson first, then three new ones. Some are ordinary jobs, because refusing everything is not the skill. Each reveal names the sign, and says which way money or your details would move: in to you from an employer, out of you to a stranger, or through your account for someone else. Only the last is money laundering, and only those reveals say that moving the money can be a crime. With JavaScript on and storage allowed, each situation you reveal joins your review on this device. One you miss comes back tomorrow; one you get right comes back later each time. Nothing you pick leaves the browser, and the page address never records it. What it does not do: it cannot check a real message, look up a company, or tell you whether a real offer is genuine. The messages, people and firms are invented, and no real employer, bank, app or regulator appears on a screen. Rules on work documents, and on contracts for under-18s, differ by country; the reveals say so where it matters.

screen.from: Office manager, the firm where you interviewed
lines: Your offer letter is ready to collect: stipend ₹12,000 a month.
Paid into your bank account on the 7th, from the firm's own account.
Bring your PAN card and bank details to the office on your joining day.

drillBank.question: You had two interviews at their office last month, and the stipend matches what they said. What do you do?

options.text: Accept, and take your details to the office on the day
options.why: You met them, pay comes from their account to you, and your details go in person. Unsure? Call the number you already had.

options.text: Refuse, because it mentions your bank details
options.why: An employer needs your account to pay you. What matters is which way the money moves.

options.text: Accept, and reply now with your PAN and account number
options.why: The letter asks for them in person. Sending them in a reply is what a fake offer is hoping for.

drillBank.cueSource: Ordinary. The cue (you met them, pay flows from the employer to you, details handed over in person) is the India lesson's own rule (in/protect-your-money/money-mule, screen d2 and check 1). A letter or message alone proves nothing: fake joining letters are sent from lookalike email accounts (Enforcement Directorate raids on a fake government job racket, Akashvani News, 8 January 2026, https://newsonair.gov.in/ed-conducts-raids-at-15-locations-across-six-states-in-connection-with-fake-government-job-scam/).

lines: You earned ₹450 today for 3 reviews.
Pay ₹1,000 to move to premium tasks.
Premium members earn ₹3,000 a day.

drillBank.question: The first ₹450 really reached your account. What do you do?

options.text: Pay the ₹1,000, since the ₹450 was real
options.why: The ₹450 was paid to win your trust. Once bigger deposits go in, they are frozen.

options.text: Pay once, and leave if the ₹3,000 does not come
options.why: Once paid, the ₹1,000 is gone either way. Deposits in these groups are frozen, not paid out.

options.text: Stop, pay nothing, and report the group
options.why: A job pays you. Paying to earn more is the sign, and the early ₹450 was the bait.

drillBank.cueSource: Ministry of Home Affairs statement on over 100 websites blocked for task-based part-time job frauds (6 December 2023): the victim is paid some commission at first, asked to invest more, and larger deposits are frozen. Read in ThePrint, https://theprint.in/india/over-100-job-fraud-websites-promising-quick-money-for-work-from-home-blocked-for-laundering-money/1874090/ and The Tribune, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/india/more-than-100-websites-blocked-for-facilitating-organised-illegal-investments-569317. The PIB copy (MHA year-end review, https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1991936) returned 403 and must be opened by a person before publishing.

lines: Selected for data entry from home, ₹18,000 a month.
No interview needed.
Pay ₹1,499 for your joining kit to start.

drillBank.question: You applied to several data-entry adverts last week. What do you do?

options.text: Pay, since ₹1,499 is small next to ₹18,000 a month
options.why: The fee is what the message is for. A real employer pays you; it does not charge you to start.

options.text: Refuse: an employer pays you, never the other way round
options.why: A fee before any work, and no interview. The government's jobs portal tells jobseekers not to pay fees to employers.

options.text: Ask them to take the ₹1,499 from your first month's pay
options.why: You would still be paying to get a job. The fee is the point of the message, not the work.

drillBank.cueSource: National Career Service, Ministry of Labour and Employment: 'NCS does not charge any fee at any stage' and 'Jobseekers should not pay fees to employers' (https://www.ncs.gov.in/, accessed 22 September 2026).

screen.from: Overseas trading company (a free email address)
lines: Local finance assistant, remote: €900 a month.
Our customers in your country pay into your own account.
Pay the money on to our suppliers the same day.

drillBank.question: The pay is a fixed salary, not a cut of what arrives. What do you do?

options.text: Refuse: a real company takes its customers' payments into its own account
options.why: Your account is the job, however the pay is dressed. Moving that money for them can be a crime, and your name is on it.

options.text: Accept, since a salary is how real jobs pay
options.why: The salary is the bait. The work is other people's money passing through your account.

options.text: Accept, but only pay on money from customers you can see
options.why: You could not check where the money came from, and every payment you send on carries your name.

drillBank.cueSource: Europol #DontBeAMule flyer (https://www.europol.europa.eu/sites/default/files/documents/lux_flyers_en.pdf, read 22 September 2026): job adverts from overseas companies seeking local or national agents; a free web-based email address not matching the company name; the job always includes using your bank account to move money; this is money laundering.

screen.from: The bakery where you did a trial shift
lines: Your apprenticeship contract is attached.
Pay on the 25th of each month, with a payslip.
Bring your tax number and bank details on your first day.

drillBank.question: You did a trial shift there last week and met the owner. What do you do?

options.text: Refuse, since it asks for your bank details
options.why: An employer needs them to pay you. Here the money comes from the bakery to you.

options.text: Sign straight away without reading it
options.why: The job is real, but read what you agree to first: the hours, the pay, and how either side can end it.

options.text: Read the contract, then sign it
options.why: A contract, a payslip, pay from the employer. Under 18, a parent or guardian usually has to agree too; it depends on your country.

drillBank.cueSource: Ordinary. The cue (a contract, a payslip, pay from the employer, bank details handed over in person) is the EU lesson's own rule (eu/credit-and-fraud/money-mule: a real employer pays from its own account and needs your IBAN). Under 18: BGB §107 (a minor needs the legal representative's consent, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__107.html) and BBiG §11 (the contract goes to the trainee and the legal representatives, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bbig_2005/__11.html), with Germany as one example; other member states differ.

screen.from: Recruiter, met in a group chat
lines: Open a new online bank account in your name.
Send us the login and the card.
€300 a month, no work needed.

drillBank.question: They say the account is only for their international clients. What do you do?

options.text: Agree, since it is a new account you would not use
options.why: It is still in your name. Every payment through it is recorded against you, and moving that money can be a crime.

options.text: Refuse, and keep any login and card to yourself
options.why: Your name and account are the job. Europol's advice: never open an account at the request of somebody you just met.

options.text: Agree, but ask for the €300 up front
options.why: Being paid first changes nothing: the money moving through the account would still carry your name.

drillBank.cueSource: Europol #DontBeAMule flyer (https://www.europol.europa.eu/sites/default/files/documents/lux_flyers_en.pdf, read 22 September 2026): launderers ask for your account number or ask you to open a new one; never open a bank account at the request of somebody you just met; do not disclose online banking login or card details.

lines: You're hired as a personal assistant.
We mailed you a check for $3,160.
Keep $260 and pay the rest to our event supplier through a payment app.

drillBank.question: You deposited it, and the money shows in your app the next day. What do you do?

options.text: Send the $2,900, since the money has arrived
options.why: Showing in your app is not a good check. Found fake weeks later, it comes back and you owe the bank $2,900.

options.text: Send half now, and the rest once it clears
options.why: Whatever you send is your own money once the check bounces, and the whole $3,160 comes back off your balance.

options.text: Send nothing, and tell your bank the check may be fake
options.why: No real employer sends a check for you to pay on. Funds showing in your account do not make it a good check.

drillBank.cueSource: FTC, How to spot, avoid, and report fake check scams (updated June 2025, https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-spot-avoid-and-report-fake-check-scams): funds showing in your account do not mean it is a good check; fakes take weeks to find and you repay the bank; personal assistant jobs are a named pattern. FTC, Job scams (updated March 2023, https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams): no honest employer sends a check to deposit and then send on part of the money.

lines: Great chat. You're hired, no call needed.
Send your Social Security number and online banking login for direct deposit.

drillBank.question: The job looked real on a big job site. What do you do?

options.text: Stop, and check the job through the company's own contact details
options.why: Hired by text with no call, and asked for a banking login, which no employer needs.

options.text: Send them, since payroll needs both
options.why: Direct deposit needs an account number on a form, never your login. With the login, someone else controls your account.

options.text: Send only the Social Security number
options.why: Sent to a stranger, it can be used for identity theft. Check the employer before any form asks for it.

drillBank.cueSource: FTC alert, That job offer text is probably a scam (30 April 2026, https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2026/04/job-offer-text-probably-scam). FTC, Job scams (updated March 2023, https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams): honest employers interview before hiring, and its warning signs include requests for personal and bank details. FTC, What to know about identity theft (updated September 2024, https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/what-know-about-identity-theft).

lines: Library assistant, $15 an hour, 10 hours a week.
Paid through the college payroll every two weeks.
Form I-9: bring your documents within three business days of starting.
You choose which ones, from the list on the form.

drillBank.question: You interviewed at the library desk on Monday. What do you do?

options.text: Accept, and bring the documents in your first days
options.why: An interview in person, pay from the college payroll, and the forms after the offer.

options.text: Refuse, since it asks for documents
options.why: Every employer completes Form I-9 with each new hire, after the offer. You pick the documents.

drillBank.cueSource: Ordinary. USCIS I-9 Central, Completing Section 2 (updated 18 September 2026, https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/completing-form-i-9/completing-section-2-employer-review-and-attestation): documents within 3 business days of starting; the employee chooses one List A document or one List B plus one List C. IRS, Hiring employees (updated 18 February 2026, https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/hiring-employees): a Form I-9 for every hire.

changes.what: Shared money helpers only; nothing tool-specific. (1) export function toCents(v: number): number: returns 0 when v is not finite; otherwise c = Math.round(Number((Math.abs(v) * 100).toPrecision(15))), returns v < 0 ? -c : c, and never -0 (c === 0 gives 0). Half away from zero on the decimal as typed. Use toPrecision(15), not the 12 in take-home-pay's spec: 12 significant digits turn yearly-rate's 999,999,999,999.99 fee into 1e14 cents and break its capped pin; every take-home pin still holds with 15. (2) export const fromCents = (c: number): number => c / 100. (3) export const roundMoney = (v: number): number => fromCents(toCents(v)). (4) export function roundTo(x: number, dp: number): number: non-finite x returned as is; a = Math.abs(x); r = String(a).includes('e') ? Math.round(a * 10 ** dp) / 10 ** dp : Number(Math.round(Number(`${a}e${dp}`)) + `e-${dp}`); returns x < 0 ? -r : r (half away from zero, no -0). (5) export const round1 = (x: number) => roundTo(x, 1); export const round2 = (x: number) => roundTo(x, 2). (6) export const toBasisPoints = (percent: number): number => Math.round(percent * 100). (7) export function divRoundHalfUp(n: number, d: number): number for integers n >= 0, d > 0: q = Math.floor(n / d), rem = n - q * d, return rem * 2 >= d ? q + 1 : q; throws RangeError when n < 0, d <= 0 or either is not an integer. (8) export function shareOf(cents: number, ratePercent: number): number = Math.round(cents * toBasisPoints(ratePercent) / 10000). (9) export function percent1(partCents: number, wholeCents: number): number | null = wholeCents > 0 ? Math.round(partCents * 1000 / wholeCents) / 10 : null. (10) Pay frequency, one allow-list for the batch: export const PAYDAYS_PER_YEAR = { weekly: 52, fortnightly: 26, 'twice-monthly': 24, monthly: 12 } as const; export type PayFrequency = keyof typeof PAYDAYS_PER_YEAR; export const PAYDAYS = PAYDAYS_PER_YEAR (the name take-home-pay's spec uses); export function isPayFrequency(v: unknown): v is PayFrequency = typeof v === 'string' && Object.hasOwn(PAYDAYS_PER_YEAR, v); export function parsePayFrequency(v: unknown, fallback: PayFrequency): PayFrequency. (11) DeductionLine gains optional subtotalLabel?: string, which deductions() ignores. deductions(start, lines) is rewritten on integer cents: currentC = toCents(start); for each line currentC -= toCents(line.amount) and running.push(fromCents(currentC)); returns { start, running, deducted: fromCents(toCents(start) - currentC), net: fromCents(currentC) }. The revised specs' tool maths (takeHome, perMonth, yearlyRate, rateSchedule, groupSchedule, minimumRun, bufferPlan, timeAway, paydayAfterPlans, housingShare, dayOneCost, tdsRefundLines, selfEmploymentSetAside, and take-home's line()) do NOT go here: each lives in its own src/lib/tools/<slug>.ts. lesson-math.ts keeps its private round2 (changing it could move a rendered lesson figure; no tool needs it).

'').trim(); '' gives { null, false }; PATTERN = /^[+-]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(e[+-]?\d+)?$/i; if text fails PATTERN, strip everything except digits, '.' and '-' and test again; still failing gives { null, false }; n = Number(text); not finite gives { null, true }; -0 becomes 0; otherwise { n, false }. export function isBlank(raw: unknown): boolean = String(raw ?? changes.what: Pure link parsing and building, used by tool-kit.tsx. export const LINK_VALUE_MAX = 24; export const CODEC_VALUE_MAX = 2000; export const CODEC_KEYS = ['rows', 'lines', 'others', 'plans'] as const (budget rows, take-home Europe lines, take-home India/US other lines, pay-later plans). export interface LinkOptions { allowed?: Partial<Record<string, readonly string[]>> }. export function parseLinkParams(hash: string, search: string, keys: readonly string[], options: LinkOptions = {}): Record<string, string>: h = new URLSearchParams(hash.replace(/^#/, '')), s = new URLSearchParams(search.replace(/^\?/, '')); for each key in keys (the trusted list from the island, never from the link): value = h.has(key) ? h.get(key) : s.get(key); skip null; max = CODEC_KEYS includes key ? CODEC_VALUE_MAX : LINK_VALUE_MAX; drop the key when value.length > max; drop it when options.allowed?.[key] exists and does not include value; a dropped key never falls back to the other source. Keys not in the list (for example 'main' from '#main', or '__proto__') are never read. export function linkFor(href: string, query: Record<string, string>): string: url = new URL(href); url.search = ''; url.hash = new URLSearchParams(query).toString(); return url.toString().
