brief.indexDesign:
TOOLS INDEX, src/pages/[region]/tools/index.astro, static HTML, no script. Data: available = await availableTools(region.code) (toolsFor in TOOLS order, minus any drill whose src/content/drills/{region}/{slug}.json is missing); groups = groupsFor(region.code, available); for each drill, situations = (await drillFor(region.code, slug)).situations.length. Head: BaseLayout title `Tools — Business Lab ${region.name}`, regionSub 'tools', path 'tools', description `${available.length} free tools for ${region.name}, grouped by moment: ${phrases}. Nothing you type leaves your browser.` where phrases are the present groups' phrase joined with ', ' and ' and ' before the last (India: 'your first pay, a buffer, borrowing, working for yourself and spotting scams'; Europe adds 'moving out' in its place). Markup, inside
: (1)
with {region.name} edition,

Tools

,

Calculators that answer one question from your own numbers, and drills of made-up screens. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.

(the clause ', and drills of made-up screens' is dropped only if the edition has no available drill), then
    with one
  • {group.title}
    • per present group, in GROUPS order: plain links in the reader's words, no questionnaire, no recommendation, no pill. (2) Per present group, in GROUPS order:

    {group.title}

      and per tool

    • {tool.answers}

      {titleFor(tool, region.code)}{toolMetaLine(tool, situations)}Open
      • . Group titles, sentence case, exactly: 'Your first pay', 'A buffer for a bad month', 'Borrowing and paying later', 'Moving out' (Europe only), 'Working for yourself', 'Before you send, sign or reply'. Membership in order: India (12) first-pay take-home-pay, budget; buffer buffer-target, savings; borrowing loan, yearly-rate, card-minimum; own-work side-hustle, break-even, side-income-tax; scams spot-the-fake ('UPI: spot the fake'), job-offer-check. Europe (11) first-pay take-home-pay, budget; buffer buffer-target, savings; borrowing loan, pay-later-payday; moving-out rent-share; own-work side-hustle, break-even; scams spot-the-fake ('Payments: spot the fake'), job-offer-check. United States (11) first-pay take-home-pay, budget; buffer buffer-target, savings; borrowing loan, card-minimum, pay-later-payday; own-work side-hustle, break-even, side-income-tax; scams job-offer-check. Meta line copy: 'Calculator, about N minutes' ('about 1 minute' when 1) or 'Drill, N situations, about N minutes', in set type at --text-sm in --muted (8.0:1 on white), no icon, pill, sticker, badge or capitals. Scoped CSS, tokens only: .tool-jumps ul { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space-2) var(--space-5); margin: var(--space-5) 0 0; } .tool-group { margin-top: var(--space-8); } .tool-group h2 { font-size: var(--text-h2); margin: 0 0 var(--space-4); } .tool-index { max-width: var(--column); } .tool-index .index-title { margin: 0; }; base.css supplies .index-row .index-meta { grid-column: 1; }. Anchor offsets come from the existing scroll-padding-top. Section sizes vary with membership, so the page is not equal stacked bands. TOOL PAGES: the crumb reads '← All tools'. EDITION FRONTS, src/pages/[region]/index.astro: the gold panel h2 becomes 'Tools that answer' and shows one giant question, tool.short, per present group, taking the first available tool of that group in TOOLS order: India 'What reaches my account?', 'When will my buffer be ready?', 'What does this loan really cost?', 'Is this worth my time?', 'Would I catch a payment scam?'; Europe the same with 'How much of my pay goes on rent and bills?' after the loan line (six lines); the United States the India five with 'Would I spot a fake job?' in the last slot. Under the list

      All {available.length} tools

      ('All 12 tools', 'All 11 tools', 'All 11 tools'), then the foot 'Calculators set up with {region.name} numbers, and drills of made-up screens. Change any number to match your own.' The hero's secondary button reads 'Open the tools'. The panel stays five or six lines at 360px and remains the one bold thing on that screen; no stat, icon or sticker is added. HOME, src/pages/index.astro: the gold panel h2 becomes 'Tools that answer'; its list is the first all-edition tool of each group (no regions field, and for a drill a bank in every edition): take-home-pay 'What reaches my account?', buffer-target 'When will my buffer be ready?', loan 'What does this loan really cost?', side-hustle 'Is this worth my time?', job-offer-check 'Would I spot a fake job?'; five lines as today, each still routed through the edition picker script; the foot 'Nothing you type leaves your phone.' is unchanged. The drill banks replace every hasDrill filter on these pages.
brief.testsPlan: Foundation gate, in order, all green before any builder starts: npm run test:unit; npm run rules; npm run build; npm run budget (every page inside its budget, the seven stub tool pages far under 90 KB; also grep dist/_astro for one CONFIG scenario string to prove config literals are not bundled into island JS); npm run contrast; npm run test:e2e (Pixel 5 and Desktop Chrome); then the ship-check screenshots at 360px and 1280px, light and dark, of /in/tools, /eu/tools, /us/tools, /in, /, in/learn/money-basics/first-payslip, in/learn/protect-your-money/cost-of-borrowing, in/tools/spot-the-fake and one stub calculator; then design-reviewer (index, panels, kit), a11y-perf-auditor (RowList focus, SelectField, jump links), security-reviewer (fragment links, parseLinkParams, readLinkParam, the fragment clearing, the codec caps) and content-reviewer (the new link and hand-off wording, the drill intros). Unit files and what they pin: finance.test.ts (toCents, fromCents, roundMoney, roundTo, round1, round2, toBasisPoints, divRoundHalfUp, shareOf, percent1, PAYDAYS_PER_YEAR, isPayFrequency, parsePayFrequency, deductions on cents with every old pin); format.test.ts (formatDuration, percentValue, ratePercent, plural); fields.test.ts (readAmount, isBlank); link-params.test.ts (hash first, query second, per-key; caps 24 and 2000; allowed lists; '#main'; prototype keys ignored; linkFor); tools.test.ts (registry order and fields, counts 12/11/11, groupsFor, titleFor, toolBySlug, lessonToolLinks, toolMetaLine, CONFIGS editions, JSON-plain configs, scenario sentences, rule shapes, glossary ids, latestAsOf, formatCheckedDate); drills.test.ts (bank parse and layout, registry coverage, fromLesson checks, mergeDrill ids and collisions, schema fixtures for duplicate and forbidden ids, denylist and .example hosts on all merged screens, intro counts, content linters, stub skips listed by name, full mix rules for complete banks); lessons.test.ts (moreTools in skip sets, tool and moreTools slugs in the edition, explorer targets in the edition; existing rules unchanged via content-rules.ts); progress.test.ts (review() and nextReturnAmong; schedule unchanged). tests/freshness/rules.freshness.test.ts runs only through npm run rules (warn at 11 months or a passed reviewBy, fail at 12). E2E: tests/e2e/tools-foundation.spec.ts (fragment links, clearing, copy link via clipboard permissions, budget # and ?, grouped index, fronts, home, edition menu subs, Pagefind kinds, scenario lines, lesson hand-offs with JS off and on, drill pages with JS off, return line, same-day re-answer in box 1, the Incoming call caption, no ordinary leak, checks.json keys); tests/e2e/a11y.spec.ts derives every tool page from the registry and the bank files; existing tools.spec.ts, tools-more.spec.ts, lessons.spec.ts, regions.spec.ts, consent.spec.ts and og.spec.ts stay unchanged and green. Per-tool stubs: tests/unit/tools/<slug>.test.ts and tests/e2e/tools/<slug>.spec.ts, replaced by each builder. Builder obligations, each in its own files only: every pin of its revised spec in tests/unit/tools/<slug>.test.ts (never finance.test.ts); its spec's e2e cases in tests/e2e/tools/<slug>.spec.ts at 360 and 1280, including a # link, an old ? link and an allow-listed select value from a link falling back; tools with edition rules add a case that sets lp:locale to another edition's locale with context.addInitScript and still sees the edition's currency, and assert their RulesLine text, links and ToolTerms; take-home-pay and pay-later-payday add the codec unit tests and keyboard-only row add/remove at 360px (focus lands on the new row's first field; removal is announced); drill builders make their banks complete so drills.test.ts shows no skip for them, and add e2e for six situations, the bank review id stored as '<edition>/tools/<slug>#<id>' and served by checks.json, and the denylist on all .mock-screen text. Release check for the integrator after all builders land: npm run ship-check green, zero skipped tests in drills.test.ts, zero it.todo in tests/unit/tools, npm run rules with no failure, CLAUDE.md counts updated, the reviewer verdicts recorded.
risks: The revised specs for pay-later-payday (from its plan-row fields on), spot-the-fake, job-offer-check, rent-share and side-income-tax were cut off in the text this brief was written from; their foundation needs were taken from the skeptics' fixes in docs/research/interactive-tools-spec.json and the registry. Each of those builders must check its revised foundationNeeds against this brief first and raise any gap with the integrator instead of editing a shared file.

This brief overrides the revised specs in four places, and builders must follow the brief: tool data and Rules go in src/lib/tools/<slug>.ts CONFIG, not regions.ts; tool maths and pins go in that module and tests/unit/tools/<slug>.test.ts, not finance.ts and finance.test.ts; toCents uses toPrecision(15), not 12 (12 breaks yearly-rate's 999,999,999,999.99 pin; every take-home pin still holds); Rule freshness is npm run rules, not a Vitest date assertion.

src/lib/tools.ts and the new src/lib/tools/ folder sit side by side. Vite and TypeScript resolve '../lib/tools' to the file first, but a stray index.ts in the folder or an import without the full path would be confusing; always import per-tool modules by their full path.

Once the foundation lands, the index, the edition fronts, the home page and 19 lessons link to seven stub calculators that say 'This calculator is being built' and to drills that show only their lesson's screens. The branch must not be merged or deployed until every builder has finished; drills.test.ts lists each stub bank as a visible skip for that reason.

The kit change touches all five existing calculators: every page now prints the link note, reads the fragment first and clears it after load, and Copy link writes a # instead of a ?. The existing ?-link, reset and currency e2e tests must stay green before merge.

Clearing the fragment means a reload shows the typed or default figures, not the shared ones, and some browsers keep the original URL in global history, so on a shared phone the figures may still appear there. Old ?links stay in the address bar by design. The link note says anyone who receives a link sees the numbers.

review() changes spaced review for lessons as well as drills: a right answer before an item is due no longer moves it up a box. Readers who redo a quiz the same day will see items return sooner than before; the dashboard's 'ready to review' figure can differ from what it showed before.

LessonLayout now fixes each explorer's hand-off by its kind. pricing-a-service and pricing-a-job's margin explorers open break-even (with their own numbers) instead of side-hustle; every lesson with a deduction or drill explorable and a tool now shows a link it did not have (for example eu/income-statement to break-even, us/paid-promotion to savings). content-reviewer should read these links.

Astro serialises each island's config into the page HTML; long hints and rule labels make the HTML heavier, and a config that holds a function, a Date or undefined fails the JSON round-trip test. Config literals must not be imported by islands as values, or they land in the JS budget.
tests/e2e/a11y.spec.ts imports src/lib/tools.ts; if anyone adds an astro:* import to the registry, Playwright cannot load it. Keep tools.ts pure.
Registry copy (title, answers, short, intro, minutes) is fixed by the foundation. A builder whose review changes that copy must ask the integrator; editing tools.ts in parallel would conflict.

cost-of-borrowing carries edits for two tools: yearly-rate's builder owns the file and makes card-minimum's source replacement (the repealed RBI id=12300 to id=13155) on its behalf. The two builders should agree the final sources list.

The real-name denylist is case-sensitive and whole-word, applied to screen.from, lines and action only; a lower-case or spaced brand ('paytm', 'G Pay'), or a coined name that happens to match a real business (the skeptics found 'Quickdeal Trading', 'Kovač Bakery', 'Brightline'), is not caught. namesCheckedOn records the manual search; content-reviewer still reads every screen. 'Brightline' is left out of the shared list because the current us/job-scam screen uses it; job-offer-check's builder renames it.
MockScreen's 'call' caption changes to 'Incoming call' on the existing upi-fraud lesson too; the 'Video call: caller in uniform' sender line carries the video detail there.

The five lessons whose second drill screen is flagged ordinary rely on their intros' counts ('One is an ordinary …'); drills.test.ts checks the bank intros, and each drill builder must rewrite its bank intro when the set grows.
The header nav still says 'Calculators' while the page it opens is titled 'Tools'; renaming the nav item is outside this brief and would need the design-reviewer.

Rule freshness now warns only when npm run rules runs (ship-check). Without a scheduled CI job, which needs Rajvir because .github/workflows is protected, a quiet branch will not flag the US wage base changing in January or India's labour-code rules.

JS budget: the kit grows by SelectField, RowList, ToolNotes and the link reader on every calculator page (an estimated 1–2 KB gzipped); npm run budget must confirm each new tool page stays under 90 KB once its island is built.
